schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE SEAM BETWEEN A SKILL AND THE LEARNING BLOCK ANATOMY — one gated call a markdown-executed skill fires to put its own firing through the door. `fire(skill, payload)` reads the skill's input contract FROM ITS CHARTER (`skills/<name>/intention+why.json`, key `input_contract`), gates the payload through the primitive's door (every lack named in one pass, the refusal itself traced), emits the exit-time finding, and berths the whole firing as one file under instance-space. A shell door (`python3 -m cairn.skill_block fire <skill> <packet.json>`) exists because the caller is an LLM reading markdown, not a python program — and that door SPLITS the two failure kinds: a packet that fails the contract is fatal (exit 2, every lack named), while a root that cannot be WRITTEN is not (exit 0, no berth printed, the loss loud on stderr). The recording never wedges the work; the downstream gate is what turns a missing berth into a refusal later. The reader half — `read_berth(path)` — is the ONE place that knows a berth's layout, so the gate that later demands a firing and the seam that wrote it cannot disagree about what a berth is.
why: A skill's executor is an LLM reading markdown, so a door the markdown ASKS to be called is policy, not physics — the skate Akien named on 2026-08-01 ('there's nothing for you to skate with' is the goal, and prose does not get there). Cairn's proven in-house answer is the chart brick's three legs: the gate refuses a malformed packet, the next stage template-fills from the previous berth, and a downstream consumer refuses without the artifact. This component is the first leg made reusable, and the third leg is wired at the same time (see buildme_rides_the_intent below) — which is what turns 'the skill should fire the door' into 'the build door does not open unless it did'. Contract-in-charter rather than contract-in-code is the load-bearing choice: it makes migrating skill #2 a charter edit with ZERO code change, which is the template claim the parent ticket is chartered on.
invoke: Import: `from cairn.skill_block import skill_block as sb` — `sb.load_contract(skill)` (reads the charter; SkillBlockRefused if the SKILL is unwired) · `sb.fire(skill, payload)` (gates, traces, emits the finding, berths; DoorRefused if the FIRING is insufficient) · `sb.read_berth(path)` (None rather than raising — the caller turns that into a finding WITH the address) · `sb.block_name(skill)` -> 'skill:<name>'. From BASH (the door skills actually use): `python3 -m cairn.skill_block fire <skill> <packet.json>` and `python3 -m cairn.skill_block contract <skill>`; exit 0 recorded, 2 refused. Prove: `python3 cairn/skill_block/proofs/test_skill_block.py` (exit 0 = green). Roots injectable: `CAIRN_SKILL_BERTHS` (berths; default ~/.cairn/devices/skill_block/0/berths) and the primitive's `CAIRN_LB_TRACE_ROOT` (traces) — every proof call passes explicit roots and never touches the live stores.
for_whom: SKILLS are the callers — /intent first (ticket intent-becomes-a-learning-block), the rest of the roster after, each by declaring an `input_contract` in its own charter. AKIEN is the gate at the far end: the finding this seam emits stands in his queue until `cairn recordverdict` names it. THE BUILD INSPECTOR is the downstream consumer — `buildme_rides_the_intent` composes `read_berth` to refuse a cast ticket's BUILDME crossing when the ticket names no /intent firing.
node_class: code-seam — the machinery is the code, one address (ticket intent-becomes-a-learning-block, child b of skills-migrate-one-blow; the seam is piece 2 of that ticket's eight).
how_it_learns: It doesn't, and the reason is structural: this is a seam, and a seam that formed an opinion about the firings crossing it would be a second gate beside the one it serves (Law 6). What learns is on either side — the primitive's verdict corpus in CairnCommons/learning/ accumulates Akien's judgments of the findings this seam emits, and each skill's own question set gains questions from its downstream rejections. The one thing this component makes learnable that was not before: the DENOMINATOR. A refused firing is traced, so 'how often does /intent's door actually red' becomes a countable number rather than an impression — which is exactly the vacuity question the intent-door-refusals watch asks.
entry: Built 2026-08-01 under the full chain (/intent -> /challenge -> /sorted -> /chart(7 berths) -> /sail). In-house precedent composed, cited not copied: the chart brick's gate+berth+consumer pattern, measured over nine instances, is the design this generalizes; the learning_block primitive supplies the door, trace and finding organs unchanged (nothing is re-implemented here); ticket_path/read_berth follow the one-implementation-two-mouths rule the chart's berth gate established; the CLI's exit-code convention and first-pass completeness are the primitive's and the ruling gate's.
state_and_history: history.json + state.json beside this charter once the seam crosses on its own address; today the voyage is journaled at skills/intent/ — the ticket is /intent's migration, and this seam is a piece of it rather than a separate voyage. Named here rather than left to inference.
filed_edges: (a) the contract lives in the skill's charter, so a skill can widen its OWN door by editing its charter — there is no second gate over contract edits. Accepted in v0: a charter is an authored artifact under Akien's ratification and the map renders it, so a loosened contract is visible; if contract-drift ever shows up in the trace (a door that stops redding right after a charter edit), the fix is a contract-change record beside the charter, not a lock here.

(b) `fire` writes the trace, the finding and the berth in three acts, not one transaction — a crash between them leaves a traced firing with no berth. Named, not papered: the trace is the record of truth (it carries the green and the refusal alike) and the berth is derivable-from-nothing, so the failure mode is a missing berth rather than a phantom one, which the gate reports by address.

(c) `read_berth` returning None collapses 'missing' and 'unparseable' — deliberately, because the caller's disposition is identical and the address travels in the finding either way. A caller that ever needs to tell them apart gets a second reader, not a widened return.

(d) the berth carries the payload MINUS bullets under `answers`, with bullets kept separate — so a skill cannot name a contract field `bullets` and quietly shadow the finding. Nothing enforces that today; it is a naming collision waiting on a second tenant to matter.

(e) NOTHING MAKES A SKILL FIRE THIS. The wire is a step in SKILL.md plus a downstream consumer that refuses without the artifact — that is the chart brick's pattern, and it is as far as physics reaches while the executor is an LLM reading markdown. The residue is honest: a skill fired and never berthed leaves no trace to count, so the denominator measures firings-that-happened, not firings-that-should-have. The ceiling is the host's prompt-type hook, same as the turn-shape scan's.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_skill_block.py, runnable bare (python3) and under the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed (git). The gate this seam SERVES (the finding at Akien's desk) is his, never this code's.
falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) a firing passes with a declared contract field empty — including an EMPTY COLLECTION, which is the absence of a value wearing the field's name; (2) a refusal names fewer than all lacks, or leaves no trace (the denominator dies with it); (3) migrating a second skill requires a source change in this component — the template claim, tested by asserting this module's own bytes are identical across two tenants' firings; (4) a berth is written that the gate's reader cannot read, or a reader exists that knows the layout independently; (5) a bullet reaches the finding tagged `hex` by hand (invented provenance); (6) an unknown `exit` value is accepted, or a routed_out firing berths without reaching the finding queue; (7) the proof writes into a live trace or berth root — a proof that pollutes the denominator it will be read against breaks its own measure; (8) an unwritable root WEDGES the calling skill (the shell door must exit 0 with no berth and a loud stderr, never a traceback) — but equally red if it exits 0 while still printing a berth path, which would hand a caller an address that does not exist.
traces_to: Law 2 (CP1-CP6 hold in the process that builds the system — the skills ARE that process)
Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics — this is the prose-to-gate move for the skill roster)
Law 6 (one owner per gate; the seam is mechanism, Akien is the gate)
Law 7 (a refusal names every lack, on the first pass, at a diagnostic surface)
cairn/learning_block/intention+why.json (the five organs this seam fires)
proof: proofs/test_skill_block.py — 24 teeth, defect-first, injected roots. The contract is read from the charter (and a skill with no charter / no contract / an empty contract is refused as UNWIRED, distinct from a firing that is insufficient); every lack in one pass; the refusal is traced; an empty bullet list is a lack, not a value; a conforming firing traces green; the ticketless kill exit reaches the finding queue; unknown exits and hand-claimed hex refused; the berth carries what the gate needs and read_berth returns None rather than raising; the CLI's exit codes are honest AND the proof is pinned off the live roots by its own tooth; A SECOND SKILL NEEDS NO CODE CHANGE (falsifier 3, tested now rather than promised — the module's bytes are compared across two tenants' firings); and six teeth on the downstream consumer: no berth reds, a real berth greens, an unresolving berth reds by address, a berth for the WRONG skill reds, a NAMED exemption passes while a blank one reds as an exemption (not as a bad path), and an unfiled ticket stays silent because the chokepoint already refuses it by name. The 24th tooth is the LIVE FIRE's: an unwritable root exits 0 with a null berth and a loud stderr, no traceback.
provenance: Cast inside ticket intent-becomes-a-learning-block (2026-08-01) as piece 2 of eight, built in the triage order the chart's berths set. The claim-direction reversal is the design find worth keeping: the chart gate globs berths for a packet CLAIMING a ticket, but /intent fires BEFORE /sorted casts, so an intent berth can never know a ticket id — the claim had to travel the other way, and the ticket names its berth. That made the field and its check one indivisible piece rather than two. Akien's ruling the same day chose physics over prose: 'no cast without /intent'. The named exemption ('none, because <why>') was not a softening — it was forced by measurement: 70 filed tickets, 0 carrying the field, 25 at or before BUILDME.
